Subject: Clarify billing for long-history sessions — bundling / minimums

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Dedicated plan looks promising. Our procurement team is running the numbers and has a few specific asks about how Redwood will meter and invoice a couple of patterns we expect at BrightCart:

1) Long-history customer support sessions that keep the full convo (~12k tokens) pinned for retrieval and occasional edits. Are those counted as active context every hour they're stored, or only when a call accesses the KV?
2) If we sign an annual committed seat for a bundle with a 50k-token monthly minimum, how does Redwood apportion that minimum across interleaved sessions vs short microcalls?
3) Rounding: we saw notes about a per-call quantum and a 1,000-token floor on invoices — how does that interact with streaming partial responses?

Procurement would like a short worked example we can attach to our SOW. If convenient, can you also include any standard concessions you make for multi-quarter commitments?

Appreciate it,

Hi Sophie — thanks for the concrete examples and the CSV, that helps. Quick answers up front and then I’ll loop in Karthik for the technical nuance and Marissa for pricing concessions.

Short answers: 
- Active-context accounting: we bill tokens when a model actively consumes them during generation (including prefix + KV), not simply for storage. There is an exception for pinned long-history contexts that we prefetch for low-latency read paths — those can incur a small warmup credit if kept continuously active.
- Minimum apportionment: the committed monthly minimum is applied at the account level, then we map invoice lines to logical conversation groups. If you have many short microcalls, we do a best-effort prefix coalescing before applying the floor, which reduces overcounting.
- Rounding/quantum: streaming partials are metered by tokens produced/consumed; we then apply the invoice quantum (default 1,000-token slab) to the aggregated line item.

I’m attaching a quick worked example spreadsheet and a one-pager that shows how the math flows (prefix reuse, KV hits, warmup credits). Karthik — could you confirm the warmup credit behavior and whether the prefetch path counts as active if the KV isn't referenced in a generation?

Marissa — Sophie asked about concession language for longer commitments.

Best,
Irene

Hi all,

Quick technical clarification from infra/serving side: 

1) Storage vs active consumption: storage alone does NOT generate token charges. Tokens are charged when the runtime materializes them into the model's context window for a generation request. That includes when we attach KV cache pages or restore prefix tokens for continuity.

2) Prefetch/warmup credits: for low-latency reads we sometimes prefetch a small set of KV blocks into GPU memory. If the prefetch happens and the session is not used within the billing window (we use 60-minute windows), we issue a warmup credit equal to the cost of those prefetched tokens (so BrightCart wouldn't be billed for warmups you never actually used). If the session is accessed, the full token consumption counts (no double-billing).

3) Coalescing logic & minimum application: we first group calls by conversation id and similarity of prefix; we attempt to coalesce prefixes within a 24h window to avoid overcounting. After coalescing, each invoice line is rounded up to the quantum (default 1,000 tokens) and then the account-level monthly minimum is applied across lines. So scenario: 20 microcalls of 50 tokens each that coalesce into a 1,000-token prefix = billed as one 1,000-token line (not 20x1,000).

Caveats: very long pinned histories (>50k) that are touched rarely may trigger a best-practice recommendation — we suggest using a retrieval-only store (no full prefix) or using a compressed embedding index to avoid keeping the whole history in prefix. We can include migration guidance.

Happy to walk through the spreadsheet and plug in your sample CSV numbers.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal, Inference Systems, Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie — thanks for the patience. Based on Karthik’s breakdown and your sample usage, here’s what we can offer for a 12-month committed arrangement (Deal BC-2026-Q1-47):

- Pricing mechanics: account-level monthly minimum of 50k tokens. Coalescing and warmup-credit rules described above apply. Invoice quantum will be set to 500 tokens (reduced from our default 1,000) for the first 6 months as a pilot to reduce rounding overhead for BrightCart.
- Concession: a 12% committed discount on per-token list rates for the first year (applies to billable tokens after coalescing).
- Credit guardrail: we’ll provide a quarterly reconciliation credit if invoice rounding results in >6% uplift vs raw token usage in that quarter (one-time quarterly true-up).
- Terms: standard SOW + procurement clause for data retention and SOC 2 addendum.

I attached a short pricing summary and a redlined SOW stub. If that all looks OK, I can convert it to a formal quote and DocuSign link by EOD tomorrow.
